examples.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
examples.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv' \, \textrm{d}x= uv - \int vu' \, \textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle  \int xe^{7x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle  \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{7x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}-\int \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}\int {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}(\frac{{e}^{7x}}{7})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{49}{e}^{7x}+C\end{aligned}
$$
